session.question: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
session.answer:
The learning curve for DIEP (Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator) breast reconstruction showed significant improvements over the studied period from July 2018 to June 2021. As the microsurgeon gained experience, there was a notable reduction in both total surgery times and flap ischemia times, reflecting improved surgical efficiency. Specifically, the average total surgery time for single DIEP procedures decreased from 296 minutes to 227.5 minutes. Concurrently, the flap ischemia time saw a reduction from 53.6 minutes to 40.9 minutes (unknownauthorsUnknownyearbreastreconstructionwith chunk 1).

In addition to these time metrics, the average length of hospital stay for patients also decreased over time, indicating enhancements in both surgical technique and postoperative care leading to enhanced patient outcomes (unknownauthorsUnknownyearbreastreconstructionwith chunk 1). This data underscores the importance of a learning curve in surgical practice, suggesting that increased experience not only improves operational efficiency but also potentially benefits patient recovery trajectories. The findings highlight the central role of practice volume in achieving optimal outcomes in complex procedures such as DIEP breast reconstruction (unknownauthorsUnknownyearbreastreconstructionwith chunk 1).
